3. ...everyone would live if they all pressed blue.

Now, let's think about the minority (i.e., those who might not follow the majority). If they press red, they'll be the only ones to survive according to the rules. But wait...

If the minority presses red, that means there are at least as many people pressing red as there are people pressing blue. This would mean that the majority is actually not a simple "blue" crowd after all.

So, in this case, if everyone were to follow the rules and press one button without knowing what others will do... the majority would still be the minority! (This is where things get tricky)

Now, I know what you're thinking: "But wait, there's a catch!" Yes, there is!

Here's my reasoning:

If I assume that everyone else will press blue (a reasonable assumption since we don't have any information about others' choices), then...

In this scenario, if the majority presses blue, and I press red, I'll be the only one to survive. This means that the minority of people who actually did press blue will die.

If, on the other hand, everyone else presses red (which is still a possible outcome), then...

I should press blue, since being part of the majority would ensure my survival in this case!

So, taking all these possibilities into account... I'll press... **blue**!
